valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 21 Nov 2026. (1) Business: an investment bank and securities dealer — government-securities primary dealer (First Capital Treasuries, 89.44% owned), corporate debt and equity trading, unit trusts (Rs 92.4bn under management), stockbroking and advisory; profit is mostly trading in fixed income, so one sector: brokerage and investment banking. (2)–(3) A financial company, so no relevering: the sector's levered beta. Damodaran's emerging-markets file (betaEmerg) couldn't be opened (pages.stern.nyu.edu blocked from this run); his January 2026 global Brokerage & Investment Banking levered beta 0.98 (623 firms, web-search extract of BetasGlobal) is used. (4) Local 5-year betas: none found. Simply Wall St 0.67 (window not stated) and TradingView 1.39 (1-year, ignored); StockAnalysis n/a. So no median of three. (5) Higher of (3) and (4): 0.98. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7)–(8) Into scripts/reinvestment.py; shown as the Required return tile. Was a hand-set cost of equity (20% / 18.5% / 17%) in the 13 Nov analysis. Refresh in January 2027 with the emerging-markets figure.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.98 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.3%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 20% / 18.5% / 17% of 13 Nov. No WACC: a dealer's borrowing (repos, short-term loans, debentures) is its raw material, so it is valued on equity.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 4% / 5% / 6%; supported 0% on 2025/26 alone (payout 147%), 4.9% through the cycle (share of profit kept 20.5% × base long-run ROE 24%). Bear and base within 2 pts; bull 6% against 7.2% at a 35% ROE.
valuationInputs.reason: scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2026 gives 0% because the Rs 7.00 dividend was 147% of EPS Rs 4.77. Over 2021/22–2025/26 dividends were Rs 34.00 a share against EPS Rs 42.78 (ten-year summary, p. 542), so about 20.5% of profit was kept; × the long-run ROE of 14% / 24% / 35% that supports 2.9% / 4.9% / 7.2%.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE
valuationInputs.reason: Company's ROE (ten-year summary, p. 542): 10.1% (2016/17), 64.4%, 0.1%, 27.3%, 47.9%, −14.1%, 46.2%, 135.8%, 59.0%, 23.2% (2025/26); median about 37%, but the high years came with big falls in bond yields (2017/18, 2020/21, 2022–2025). Years without that: 10%, 0%, −14%, and −27% over the twelve months to September 2026 (calculated). Base set at 24%, well below the median; bear near the cost of equity; bull at the ten-year average less the 2023/24 outlier. Unchanged from 13 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Same in every method; below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity, and within the supported 2.9% / 4.9% / 7.2% (Growth check). Was 5% / 6% / 7% on 13 Nov, which ran ahead of what the payout leaves to grow on.

valuationInputs.name: Normalised EPS
valuationInputs.reason: Next year's EPS is no guide: the last four quarters lost Rs 6.28 a share (calculated; latest quarter × 4 = −Rs 5.56). So the P/E and dividend methods use mid-cycle earnings = NAV Rs 16.42 (30 Sep 2026) × 14% / 24% / 35%.

valuationInputs.name: Normalised EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: Year-end P/E (price ÷ EPS, ten-year summary): 5.5x (2022/23), 1.6x (2023/24), 3.0x (2024/25), 11.1x (2025/26, p. 54); the market pays little for peak earnings. Each is at or below the justified P/E (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g): 4.3x / 6.0x / 8.2x.

valuationInputs.name: Dividends
valuationInputs.value: Next year Rs 0 / 1.00 / 3.00, growing 4% / 5% / 6%; after five years the payout becomes 1 − g ÷ ROE (71% / 79% / 83%) of normalised EPS
valuationInputs.reason: Nothing declared for 2026/27 by September 2026 after a Rs 1.21bn half-year loss; Rs 7.00 for 2025/26, Rs 7.50 for 2024/25, nothing for 2021/22 (the last loss year). Retained earnings were Rs 3.56bn (Rs 8.78 a share) at 30 Sep 2026 (p. 6). Five-year payout 79% (Rs 34.00 ÷ Rs 42.78).

valuationInputs.name: Residual income path
valuationInputs.value: ROE from the last twelve months (−27.2%, calculated) back to 14% / 24% / 35% over three years; payout 79%
valuationInputs.reason: Twelve months to September 2026: loss to shareholders Rs 2.54bn on average equity of Rs 9.34bn (calculated). A straight-line recovery over three years (the 2022 loss was followed by 46% the next year) means the next twelve months still lose about 10% of equity in the base case. Payout = five-year average (Rs 34.00 ÷ Rs 42.78).

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Justified P/B, P/E on normalised earnings, dividend model, residual income
valuationInputs.reason: A leveraged securities dealer: book value and return on equity drive the value; no cash-flow DCF (CLAUDE.md: banks and finance companies).
